Oracle Fusion 26D opt-in expiration list, in plain English

Oracle's Current Opt-In Expirations list names 23 features whose opt-in period ends with the 26D update. From 26D they are standard features: 9 are switched on for everyone, and 14 need setup before anyone can use them. By area: 19 across Financials, Projects, Procurement and Supply Chain, 2 in Permitting and Licensing, 2 in Sales.

26D is the next Oracle Fusion Cloud quarterly update. Oracle can update this list, and we recheck it every week.

What this means, in plain English

  • An opt-in expiration means Oracle first delivered the feature as something you had to opt in to. With the update in Oracle's list, the opt-in step is removed and the feature becomes part of the standard product.
  • "Now enabled: Yes" (9 here): the feature is on for all users from 26D. Nothing to switch on, but test it, because users will see it.
  • "Now enabled: No" (14 here): nothing changes for users until you do the setup on the linked Oracle page.
  • Already opted in? Per Oracle, if you opted in earlier and finished the setup, there's nothing more to do.

What else to expect in 26D

When it arrives

Oracle updates environments in cohorts. Per Oracle, Cohort A gets quarterly updates in February, May, August and November, Cohort B in March, June, September and December, and Cohort C in April, July, October and January. Test environments update on the first Friday of the update month and production two weeks later, on the third Friday. Your cohort is shown in the Oracle Cloud Console. Source: Oracle Fusion Insider, "Quarterly updates made easy"
